sections.h2: Where to take a deed in Greene County
sections.html:
The county Recorder of Deeds is at 940 N Boonville Ave, Springfield, MO 65802, and the phone is (417) 868-4068. The counter serves the public Monday to Friday from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, except county holidays, though recording intake stops earlier in the afternoon (see the cutoff section below).

The Assessor shares the building in Room 35, phone (417) 868-4101, which helps when a deed needs a legal description. The Assessor's Public Access website lists a parcel's owner, taxing district and school district and refreshes nightly, so a recent purchase may already appear.

The recorder keeps the property records for Greene County: deeds, mortgages and deeds of trust, releases and other papers that touch land. RSMo 442.380 directs that a conveyance be recorded in the county where the real estate lies, which sends your deed to this counter.

The office has three other jobs:

  • Issuing and maintaining marriage licenses
  • Filing federal and state tax liens
  • Keeping military discharge records, with a request form and regulations posted online

Drafting is not one of them. The office does not prepare documents and sends anyone changing ownership to a title company or an attorney.

The posted schedule charges $26.00 for page one of a real estate document and $3.00 for each page after that. If you want the original returned by mail, enclose a stamped return envelope or add postage to your payment.

Greene County recording charges
Document or serviceCharge
Deed or other real estate paper, page one$26.00
Same, each page after the first$3.00
Plat or survey, page one (to 18 by 24 inches)$46.00
Plat or survey, each further page$25.00

Senate Bill 938 adds $2 to the charge for real estate documents, plats and surveys, so phone the office for the current total. The state's own piece is set in RSMo 59.319: a six dollar user fee on every recorded instrument, on top of whatever else the office charges.

sections.h2: What makes a deed fit to record
sections.html:
Under RSMo 59.310 the recorder may refuse a paper that breaks the layout rules, or take it for an extra $25. Treat the list as a checklist for your title company:

  • Single-sided, unbound pages in dark ink, with type of at least eight points, on light paper of twenty-pound weight or more
  • A blank three-inch band across the top of page one for the recorder's certification, and three-quarter inch margins on all sides
  • Under the blank band: title, date, grantors with marital status, grantees, statutory addresses and the legal description

RSMo 59.330 adds two demands. The deed needs a legal description, and unless it is an easement or right-of-way it must give a mailing address for one of the grantees. A refused paper goes back to whoever presented it, with the reason in writing.

sections.h2: Packing a deed for the counter
sections.html:
Before you drive to Springfield, run through this list. Is the legal description copied exactly from the vesting deed? Is there a mailing address for at least one grantee, unless the paper is an easement or right-of-way? Do the margins and ink match the rules above? Is the fee worked out from the page count, with a stamped return envelope or postage added if you want the original mailed back?

A single missed item sends the paper back, and the office will not fix it for you. The staff cannot draft or edit a deed, so questions about wording belong with a title company or attorney. Ask them to read the packet once more the day before.

An heir selling an inherited house or an owner with tenants in place should raise those facts with the title company early, since the order in which papers are recorded can matter. A cash buyer's closing agent handles the same recording steps and pays the fees from the closing funds.

Each business day the intake window shuts at 4:00 PM, half an hour before the counters close. Anyone already at the counter by then is served. Later arrivals are recorded when the doors open at 8:00 AM the next business day. The recorder asks filers to leave staff time to check the pages.

A recorded deed does not have to state the selling price, and the fee schedule above lists no transfer tax. Ask the title company about any other closing charges.

If your closing is on a tight schedule, deliver the deed in the morning. A paper refused late in the afternoon has no time left to be fixed and recorded that day.

sections.h2: Researching a recorded paper or lien
sections.html:
The index does not work from street addresses. It answers to a full legal description, a book and page, a name or a document number. With only an address in hand, ask the Assessor for the legal description first.

The law bars the recorder from running lien searches, and liens are filed in places besides this office. Staff will still help you page through the records. A subscription service lets you download raw data, though it does not show images online. For a Greene County sale, rely on the title company's full search.

Recorded documents are $1.00 a page to copy, certification is another $1.00, and a plat copy is $5.00. A certified marriage license copy is $9.00, and a mailed request for one needs a cashier's check or money order, because personal checks are not taken.

Bring or send whatever the index needs. A legal description, book and page, name or document number will find the instrument, and the fee is counted by page.

sections.h2: How recording closes out a home sale
sections.html:
Recording is the last step. After closing, the signed deed goes to 940 N Boonville Ave and is entered in the county record. The Assessor then updates its tax maps from the warranty deeds the recorder sends over, which is why lot lines and owner names in the county's parcel data follow your deed.

A few days before signing, ask your closing agent to read the legal description, the grantee mailing address and the margins. The recorder's office does not prepare papers and points owners to a title company or attorney for any ownership change.

Springfield is the seat and largest city of Greene County, in the Ozark foothills of southwest Missouri. The county had an estimated 309,286 residents in July 2025, up from 298,915 in the 2020 count. It has 142,405 housing units, and owners live in 57.5 percent of homes. The median owned home is valued at $221,300 and median gross rent is $989. The county issued 966 building permits in 2025, so recordings come steadily from new construction and resales alike.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax on a Greene County deed?
faqs.a: The fee schedule shows none, and the recorder's FAQ says the selling price need not appear on a recorded deed. Page-based recording charges apply. Ask the title company about other closing costs.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff time to record a deed in Greene County?
faqs.a: 4:00 PM on a business day. Papers presented later are recorded starting at 8:00 AM the next business day.

faqs.q: Will the Greene County recorder tell me about liens on my house?
faqs.a: No. The law bars the office from running lien searches, and liens may be filed elsewhere. A title company's search is the reliable check before closing.

faqs.q: Where do I get a legal description for a Greene County parcel?
faqs.a: From the Assessor, Room 35 at 940 N Boonville Ave, or its Public Access website. The recorder cannot search by street address.

faqs.q: What if the recorder refuses my deed?
faqs.a: It comes back to you with the reason. A paper that misses the layout rules in RSMo 59.310 can instead be recorded for an extra $25.
